FOREWORD This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Agricultural Tractors and Power Tillers Sectional Committee had been lpproved by the Food and Agriculture Division Council. Turning and clearance diameter of agricultural tractors are important parameters which an operator should know while operating a tractor. This standard has been published to illustrate detailed method of test for determination of these diameters. This standard was first published in 1986 and was based on ISO 789-3: 1982 `Agricultural tractors -- Test procedures -- Part 3 : Turning and clearance diameter' issued by the International Organization for Standardization (1S0). With the revision of1S0789-3 in 1993, it has been decided to revise this standard also. In reporting the result of a test, made in accordance with this standard,if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS 2: 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)'.

IS 11859:2004

Indian Standard

AGRICULTURAL TRACTORS -- TURNING AND CLEARANCE DIAMETERS METHODS OF TEST ( First Revision)
1 SCOPE This standard specifies a method of determining the turning and clearance diameters of wheeled agricultural tractors. It applies to wheeled agricultural tractors having at least two axles fitted with pneumatic tyres. 2 REFERENCE The standard given below contains provisions which through reference in this text, constitutes provisions of this standard. At the time of publication, the edition indicated was valid. All standards are subject to revision and parties to agreements based on this standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent edition of the standard indicated below: IS No. 12363:1988 3 DEFINITIONS For the purposes of this standard, definitions shall apply. the following Title Recommendation on track width of agricultural tractors

--

In the case of a tractor equipped with a rear tandem, it is the distance between two vertical planes passing through the centres of the front wheel and the vertical plane midway between the wheel centres of the two axles of the tandem. 3.4 Turning Diameter -- Diameter of the circular path described by the centre of tyre contact with the surface of the test site of the wheel describing the largest circle when the tractor is executing its sharpest possible turn under the test conditions described in 5 ($ee Fig. 2). 3.5 Clearance Diameter -- Diameter of the smallest circle which will enclose the outermost points of projection of the tractor and its equipment while executing its sharpest possible turn (see Fig. 2). 4 APPARATUS 4.1 Tape Measures, of length greater than the turning and clearance diameters to be measured, having a tolerance within i 0.5 percent. 4.2 Plumb-Line, diameters. 5 GENERAL 5.1 Test Area The test area shall be a compacted or paved dry surface affording good tyre adhesion, capable of displaying legible markings, and resistant to defacement by turning machines. The test surface shall be visually flat, with no more than 3 percent grade in any direction. 5.2 Tractor Test Requirements 5.2.1 Tyre and Wheel Equipment The tractor to be tested shall be in its operating state, and the attachments with which it is equipped and their positions shall be noted. The tyre, wheel commonly used intended, that is shall be stated and fender equipment shall be that in the country for which the tractor is as specified by the manufacturer, and in the test report. Generally dual if required, for measuring clearance

3.1 Agricultural Tractor -- Self-propelled wheeled machine having at least two axles, particularly designed to pull, push, carry and operate implements used for agricultural work (including forestry work), which may be provided with a detachable loading platform. 3.2 Track (Tread) of Wheeled Tractor -- Distance at ground level between two vertical planes passing through the centreline of ground contact of the tyres parallel to the median plane of the tractor with the wheels in the straight ahead position (see Fig. 1). In the case of dual wheels it is the distance at ground level between two planes passing through the centreline of the dual wheels. 3.3 Wheel Base -- Distance at ground level between two vertical planes passing through the centres of the front wheels and the rear wheels with tractor and wheels in the same straight ahead position (see Fig. 1).

wheeled tractors or tractors with added ballast should rtot be tested unless it is the only specification presented by the manufacturer. Tyre pressures, tractor ballast and use of duals on front or rear shall be recorded in the test report. If steering and/or axle oscillation stops and fenders are part of standard equipment then these shall be positioned according to the manufacturer's instructions. All the tyres shall be inflated to the pressure specified by the manufacturer for transport work. The inflation pressure of tyres of same axle shall be ensured to be equal, 5.2.2 Track (Tread) Setting

5.2.3

Other Settings

Tractors which have all wheels steerable, or which incorporate devices for disconnecting either or both axles, shall be tested in each operating condition in which the tractor is intended to be used. Results shall be recorded for each operating condition. Tractors which have more than one powered axle, and which have devices for disconnecting the power to any of the axles, shall be tested in each operating condition in which the tractor is intended to be used. Results shall be recorded for each operating condition. 6 PROCEDURE 6.1 Right-Hand Turn, Without Brakes

Measurement of turning and clearance diameter may be made with standard track settings as specified by the manufacturer (see IS 12363). Additional measurements may be made at other track settings, if requested by the manufacturer as optional.

6.1.1 Drive the tractor slowly forward while making its sharpest possible right-hand turn, that is, with the steering kept on full right-hand lock, at a speed not

2

IS 11859:2004
A /

13G.2 TRACTOR TURNING CONFIGURATIONS

exceeding 2 km/h for at least one complete turn, until it is established that the minimum turning circle is being described. 6.1.2 Continue todrive thetractor slowly forwardon the same lock for a further complete turn, at a speed not exceeding 2 km/h. At short regular intervals around the turn, mark on the ground those poirrts coinciding with the centre of the tyre-to-ground contact area of the outermost wheel. Make the marks immediately behind this contact area and determine the position of each mark by visually projecting vertically downwards from the centre of the tyre tread width at points on the tyre circumference situated as close as possible to the ground. The marking may be done with or without stopping the tractor. The broken circle formed by the marks on the ground is the turning circle. 6;1.3 During -the turn described in 6.1.2, stop the tractor and drop a plumb-line to the ground from the outermost point of the tractor (that is, form the point of the tractor describing the largest circle). Clearly mark the point on the ground beneath the plumb-line: this point lies on the tractor clearance circle. 6.1.4 Measure the diameter of the turning circle (see 6.1.2) at a minimum of three places spaced 3

approximately equally around the circle. Calculate the average value of the diameter measured and report it as the minimum turning diameter, right-hand, without brakes. Alternatively, the diameter of the turning circle may be calculated as shown in Fig. 3 and reported in the same way. 6.1.5 Measure and record the radial distance between the point on the tractor clearance circle (see 6.1.3) and the circumference of the tractor turning circle (see 6.1.2). Add twice this dimension to the minimum turning diameter and report the result as the minimum clearance diameter, right-hand, without brakes. 6.2 Left-Hand Turn, Without Brakes

Repeat the procedures described in 6.1 with the tractor driven forward while making its sharpest possible left-hand turn, that is, with the string kept on full left-hand lock. Report the results as the `minimum turning/clearance diameter, left-hand, without brakes'. 6.3 Right-Hand Turn, with Brakes

Where applicable, repeat the procedure described in 6.1 with the inside non-steered wheel brake applied with a pedal effort sufficient to lock the wheel, subject to a maximum of 60 daN.

Where applicable, repeat the procedure described in 6.3 with the tractor making its sharpest possible left-hand turn, that is, with the steering kep~ on full left-hand lock. Report the results as the minimum diameter, left-hand, with brakes. 7 TEST REPORT
